sources: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement; Abbas Araghchi (ISNA/Telegram); Xinhua
fault_line: Can China move Iran where the US cannot -- or is Beijing just buying discounted oil while Washington does the fighting? (10K-like Hindi commentator reel on China warning citizens to leave Iran)

sections.what_happened: Araghchi met Wang Yi in Beijing (first in-person China visit since the war began Feb 28). Chinese MFA: China considers 'a complete cessation of fighting must be achieved without delay', restarting hostilities 'even more unacceptable', negotiations 'essential'; Wang called on Iran and the US to reopen the Strait of Hormuz 'as soon as possible'. Araghchi: 'We will do our best to protect our legitimate rights and interests in the negotiations... We only accept a fair and comprehensive agreement'; cooperation with China 'will even become stronger'. Dating note: AJE newsfeed item published 2026-10-24T00:57Z frames arrival; Xinhua-cited meeting reported as Wednesday (Oct 21) in the day-68 roundup -- exact arrival/meeting day unresolved, but the visit and MFA readout are confirmed this week.
sections.what_verified: Xinhua reported the meeting; Chinese MFA statement quoted verbatim by Al Jazeera; Araghchi's remarks carried by ISNA/IRNA. Three distinct publisher families (Qatari AJE, Chinese state Xinhua, Iranian state IRNA/ISNA), each state-flagged, consistent on the core facts. Not yet independently carried by Reuters/AP in this window.
sections.what_disputed: Washington has pressed Beijing to lean on Tehran to open Hormuz; analysts note Beijing's willingness is constrained by its own confrontation with Washington (Al Jazeera analysis, attributed).
sections.why_matters: While Trump demands Hormuz reopened, Iran's foreign minister went to the one capital that actually keeps Tehran afloat -- and Beijing answered with oil, not pressure.
sections.context: Background: NEW (big-missed; visit this week, first China trip since Feb 28) -- FM Abbas Araghchi in Beijing for talks with Wang Yi; China calls for complete cessation of fighting and for Iran-US to reopen Hormuz 'as soon as possible'; Araghchi: Iran will 'only accept a fair and comprehensive agreement'

totw_analysis: Our read: While Trump demands Hormuz reopened, Iran's foreign minister went to the one capital that actually keeps Tehran afloat -- and Beijing answered with oil, not pressure. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Can China move Iran where the US cannot -- or is Beijing just buying discounted oil while Washington does the fighting?
